summary: While Babylon's army surrounded Jerusalem, God told Jeremiah to buy a field as a sign that one day people would buy and sell land there again. Sabbath Camp looks back at Jeremiah's story of faithfulness.

story_reel.narration: Welcome to Sabbath Camp! While Babylon's army was surrounding Jerusalem, Jeremiah was locked up in the palace guardhouse. Then God told him something strange: 'Your cousin is going to come and ask you to buy his field in your hometown. Buy it.' Sure enough, his cousin came. Jeremiah bought the field, signed the deed in front of witnesses, and told Baruch, 'Put these papers in a clay jar so they will last a long time.' Why buy land when the enemy is about to take over everything? Because God said, 'Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.' Buying that field was a sign of hope! Jeremiah prayed, 'Ah, Lord Yahweh! You made the heavens and the earth by Your great power. Nothing is too hard for You!' Let's remember this week. God called young Jeremiah and said, 'I am with you.' Jeremiah watched the potter reshape the clay. A king burned God's Word, but it was written again. Ebed-Melech rescued Jeremiah from a muddy pit. Jerusalem fell, but Jeremiah found that God's mercies are new every morning. And he wrote a letter telling the exiles to bloom where they were planted. This week's big truth: Yahweh has good plans for you, even in hard times. Jeremiah stayed faithful for forty years, because he trusted God's plans.

memory_verse.text: "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you," says Yahweh, "thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future."
